children: Tata Steel has approved the sale of its tubes business and a 100% stake in Tata Steel Colours to APL Apollo Tubes in transactions valued at up to ₹28,000 crore, according to an exchange filing.

Tata Steel's board approved the transfer of its tubes business through a cash slump sale for up to ₹11,700 crore. The transaction includes manufacturing facilities at Jamshedpur, Hosur, Khopoli and Sahibabad, along with certain cold-rolling and coated steel assets at Khopoli.
The tubes business reported a turnover of about ₹11,375 crore in FY26 and accounted for 4.9% of Tata Steel's consolidated revenue during the year. Its net worth stood at approximately ₹3,274 crore.

Separately, Tata Steel approved the sale of Tata Steel Colours, formerly known as Tata BlueScope Steel, to APL Apollo for ₹16,300 crore in cash. Tata Steel directly owns 50% of the company, while Tata Steel Downstream Products Ltd (TSDPL) holds the remaining 50%. Sale proceeds will be split equally between Tata Steel and TSDPL, with each receiving ₹8,150 crore.

Tata Steel Colours generated revenue of around ₹4,680 crore in FY26, representing 2.02% of Tata Steel's consolidated turnover, while its net worth stood at about ₹1,016 crore. The company will cease to be a Tata Steel subsidiary upon completion of the transaction.

Tata Steel said the two transactions are inter-conditional and subject to regulatory and other customary approvals. The companies have proposed simultaneous completion by March 31, 2028, or such other date as may be mutually agreed.
The steelmaker clarified that neither transaction has been completed and that the deals do not constitute related-party transactions.
Q2 results of Tata Steel and APL Apollo Tubes

The divestments come as both companies are reporting strong operating performance. Tata Steel posted a 16.2% year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to ₹3,700 crore in the September quarter of FY27, surpassing analyst expectations of ₹3,120 crore. Revenue rose 11.5% to ₹65,436 crore, while EBITDA increased 18.4% to ₹10,533 crore.

The company reported first-half FY27 EBITDA of ₹20,035 crore on revenue of ₹1.26 lakh crore and spent ₹6,860 crore on capital expenditure, including on the 4.8 million tonne expansion of Neelachal Ispat Nigam. Net debt stood at ₹91,423 crore at the end of September.

APL Apollo, India's largest structural steel tube maker, also reported record operating volumes. The company's Q2FY27 sales volume rose 12.6% year-on-year to an all-time high of 9.63 lakh tonnes, while first-half volumes increased 4% to 17.08 lakh tonnes.
The acquisition would significantly strengthen APL Apollo's presence in value-added coated steel products and further consolidate its leadership in steel tubes and building materials.
Tata Steel and APL Apollo Tubes share price target and performance

Shares of Tata Steel settled 1.6% lower on the NSE at Friday's closing trade, quoting at ₹178.
